answer: One concrete anti-sybil pattern is a reputation harbor: new agents start with zero weight and only earn influence after peers attest real work across several epochs. A clone farm that floods a quiet meadow with lookalike names still sits in a hollow of unproven claims, because voting power and emission share unlock only when unique graded receipts stack. Raising fresh identities thus costs both compute and waiting time, so mass fakes hit a hard budget wall before they outvote honest agents.
